title: Sakkarai Pongal (sweet pongal)
story: Growing up in Nanganallur, in Chennai, I used to visit the temples in my hometown all the time. Every visit ended the same way: someone would hand me hot sakkarai pongal as prasadam in a donnai, the little leaf cup, with the ghee just flowing over the sides.
Later, during my college days in Thanjavur, I visited so many temples down south, in Thanjavur, Kumbakonam and other places. Different temples, same hot sweet pongal, same donnai, same ghee.
Even today, every time I have it, it brings back fond memories of growing up in South India. So here is my recipe for sakkarai pongal.
ingredients: 1 pinch edible camphor (pachai karpooram), only the edible kind, not aarti camphor
steps: Pressure cook the rice separately, 1 part rice to 4 parts water.
Pressure cook the moong dal with the pitted dates, again 1 part dal to 4 parts water. Both should come out really soft.
Roughly chop the jaggery, put it in a large pan with 1 cup of water, and stir over medium flame until it melts and starts to thicken, about 5 minutes.
Add the rice and dal a little at a time, alternating, until it's all in. Keep mixing for 5 to 7 minutes.
Add about three-quarters of the ghee and mix well.
Add the cardamom, a pinch of camphor and a little salt. Make sure the dates are fully mashed in.
In a small pan, heat the rest of the ghee and roast the cashews to a mild gold. Add the raisins, and once they puff up, pour it all over the pongal and mix well.
tip: The dates are what give this pongal its color and its distinct taste. That's a trick I learned from my grandmother.
closing: That's it. The sakkarai pongal is ready.

nutrition.yield: Makes about 3.4 kg, roughly 34 servings of 100 g or about 22 prasadam bowls of 150 g (about 300 kcal each).
